questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Vector Analogy?
questions.answer: Fourier analysis works like resolving a vector into perpendicular components. Sine and cosine functions act like basis directions, and coefficients measure how far the function points along each direction.

questions.prompt: What does \(\mathbf v\) mean in Vector Analogy?
questions.answer: In Vector Analogy, \(\mathbf v\) means ordinary vector.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Vector Analogy.

questions.prompt: Explain why a vibration signal can be described by mode amplitudes.
questions.answer: A vector is described by components along perpendicular axes. A vibration signal is described by components along perpendicular sine and cosine modes. The coefficient a_n is found by projecting the signal onto cos nx: \[a_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos nx\,dx\]

questions.prompt: Why does cos x not contribute to the cos 2x coefficient?
questions.answer: The modes are orthogonal over a full period: \[\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos x\cos2x\,dx=0\] The projection onto cos 2x is therefore zero, just as a vector perpendicular to an axis has zero component along that axis.
